name: mcp-zotero
description: Unofficial Zotero integration: search your library, add papers by DOI, import PDFs, read full text and inject live Zotero citations into Word documents.
long_description:
Gives Claude access to your Zotero library through the Zotero Web API: search and browse collections, add items by DOI (with open-access PDFs found via Unpaywall) or from metadata, import PDFs, read the full text indexed by Zotero, and turn `<zcite>` placeholders in a .docx file into native Zotero citations that Zotero for Word can refresh.

You need a Zotero API key (zotero.org/settings/keys, with library read/write and file access) and your numeric user ID, shown on the same page. Deletions are disabled unless you change *Deletions allowed*. To work on a group library, set *Library type* to `group` and *Group library ID*.

This is an unofficial community project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the Zotero team or the Corporation for Digital Scholarship. "Zotero" is a registered trademark of the Corporation for Digital Scholarship.

tools.description: Get the full metadata of several items at once.

tools.name: search_library
tools.description: Search the library or list items sorted by a field.

tools.name: create_collection
tools.description: Create a collection, optionally inside another one.

tools.name: add_items_by_doi
tools.description: Add items by DOI, with open-access PDFs when available.

tools.name: inject_citations
tools.description: Turn <zcite> placeholders in a .docx or .odt file into live Zotero citations.

tools.name: create_cited_document
tools.description: Create a .docx or .odt from Markdown with live Zotero citations and a bibliography.

tools.name: get_item_fulltext
tools.description: Read the full text Zotero has indexed for an item's PDF.

tools.name: get_user_id
tools.description: Show the configured library (user or group) and its ID.

tools.name: add_linked_url_attachment
tools.description: Attach a link to a web page or file to an item.

tools.name: add_items
tools.description: Add items from metadata, for any Zotero item type (e.g. items without a DOI).

tools.name: update_item
tools.description: Edit an existing item's fields or creators (needs its current version).

tools.name: create_note
tools.description: Attach a plain-text note to an existing item.

tools.name: import_pdf_to_zotero
tools.description: Download a PDF from a URL and store it in Zotero.

tools.description: Find open-access PDFs for existing items and attach them.

tools.name: delete_collection
tools.description: Delete a collection, keeping its items (needs deletions set to 'all').

tools.description: Permanently delete items (needs deletions set to 'items' or 'all').

prompts.name: cite_word_document
prompts.description: Turn the <zcite> placeholders in an existing .docx (or .odt) into live Zotero citations and a bibliography.
prompts.text:
I have a Word document at ${arguments.file_path} and I want to add Zotero citations to it.

Please:
1. Make sure each place a citation should appear contains a <zcite keys="ITEMKEY"/> placeholder in its own text run (keys are Zotero item keys from search_library, add_items or add_items_by_doi). For a numbered style (ieee/vancouver) every <zcite> also needs a num attribute, numbered in order of first appearance.
2. Call inject_citations with file_path "${arguments.file_path}" and style "${arguments.style}". It fetches the metadata from Zotero and writes a new <name>_cited file next to the original.
3. Tell me to open the result in Word with the Zotero plugin and run Zotero → Refresh, so the citations become editable.

prompts.name: write_cited_document
prompts.description: Draft a document on a topic with inline Zotero citations and a bibliography, saved as .docx or .odt.
prompts.text:
Write a well-structured document about "${arguments.topic}" with Zotero citations, and save it to ${arguments.output_path} as ${arguments.format}.

Please:
1. Gather the references in Zotero first: add_items_by_doi for items with a DOI, add_items for the rest, or search_library to reuse items already in the library. Keep track of each item key.
2. Write the body as Markdown and cite sources inline with pandoc-style keys: [@ITEMKEY] for one source, [@KEY1; @KEY2] for several, [see @ITEMKEY, p. 12] with a locator, and -@ITEMKEY to suppress the author.
3. Call create_cited_document with that Markdown as the markdown argument, output_path "${arguments.output_path}", format "${arguments.format}" and style "${arguments.style}". It resolves the citations against Zotero, numbers them in order of first appearance and appends the bibliography.
4. Tell me the citations are live Zotero fields: open the result in Word or LibreOffice with the Zotero plugin and run Refresh to edit them.

prompts.name: import_references
prompts.description: Add one or more references to Zotero from their DOIs, attaching open-access PDFs when available.
prompts.text:
Import these references into Zotero by DOI: ${arguments.dois}

Please call add_items_by_doi with the list of DOIs (strip any surrounding text, keep only the bare DOIs). It resolves the metadata automatically and attaches an open-access PDF when one is found. Report which DOIs were added and which failed, and suggest add_items for anything without a usable DOI.

prompts.name: note_from_item
prompts.description: Read an existing Zotero item and attach a concise summary as a child note.
prompts.text:
Read the Zotero item ${arguments.item_key} and attach a short summary note to it.

Please:
1. Fetch the item with get_items_details (item_keys ["${arguments.item_key}"], include_abstract true); if it has a PDF, get_item_fulltext for more detail.
2. Write a concise plain-text summary (key points, method, findings) and attach it with create_note (parent_item_key "${arguments.item_key}"). Use blank lines between paragraphs; no HTML or Markdown.

zotero_api_key.title: Zotero API key
zotero_api_key.description: Create one at zotero.org/settings/keys with library read/write and file access.

zotero_user_id.title: Zotero user ID
zotero_user_id.description: Your numeric user ID, shown on zotero.org/settings/keys (it is not your username).

zotero_library_id.title: Group library ID
zotero_library_id.description: Numeric group ID, required when the library type is 'group'. Leave empty for your personal library.

unpaywall_email.title: Email for Unpaywall
unpaywall_email.description: Optional. Sent to the Unpaywall API to find open-access PDFs when adding papers by DOI; leave empty to skip the PDF lookup.

unsafe_operations.title: Deletions allowed
unsafe_operations.description: 'none' (default): deletions disabled. 'items': enables delete_items (permanent: deleted items do not go to the Zotero trash). 'all': enables delete_items and delete_collection (the items of a deleted collection stay in the library).
